question: Explain why the conductivity of a semiconductor increases with increase in temperature, whereas the conductivity of a metal decreases. Justify your answer using the concept of charge carriers.

options.A: In a semiconductor, increasing temperature reduces electron-hole pairs, so conductivity decreases. In a metal, heating creates many new electrons, so conductivity increases.
options.B: The conductivity of both semiconductors and metals always increases with temperature because carrier collisions decrease.
options.C: In semiconductors and metals, conductivity is independent of temperature because charge-carrier concentration never changes.
options.D: A semiconductor has a small band gap; heating creates more electron-hole pairs, increasing the number of mobile carriers and hence conductivity. A metal already has many free electrons; heating increases lattice vibrations and collisions, reducing electron mobility and therefore decreasing conductivity.
